assertions.assert: It waits in `intake` for `builder.request` `{spec, name?, constraints?, max_attempts?, model?, generate_timeout_ms?, generate_ceiling_ms?, min_every_ms?, turn_after_bound_ms?, apply?, template?}`; data its schema refuses is refused at the sender (its send raises `error.execution` there) and the builder keeps waiting; a request whose spec is only whitespace ends in the final state `failed` with `{reason: "invalid-request", diagnostics: [{kind: "request", code: "invalid-request"}]}`, which the invoker receives as `done.invoke.<id>`.

A request is planned (`design`, schema `topology_plan`), authored (`author`, schema `scxml_draft`: its `scxml`, `schemas` and `script`), written as `<name>.scx`, `<name>.json` and `<name>.js` through the files service (`writing`; the request's `name`, else the plan's; decision D121), validated (`validate`) and simulated (`simulate`, each test script driving the draft as an invoked child by `srcexpr` on its path); a draft that validates and passes every test ends in the final state `done` with `{scxml, schemas, script, path, tests, report: {attempts, failures, fixes_applied, warnings, plan, decisions, history, simulation}}`, `path` `../../behaviors/<name>.scx`.
A draft whose validator errors all have machine-applicable fixes is fixed (`apply_fixes`, at most 2 passes per draft) and validated again, without a new attempt: `report.fixes_applied` counts it.

Every failure goes through `retry_gate`, then `triage`, which asks the decision service to choose among its enabled transitions: `triage.repair` authors the draft again from the same plan (`report.decisions` `["triage.repair"]`), `triage.redesign` plans again, `triage.abandon` ends in `failed` `{reason: "abandoned"}`. When the decision is unavailable it falls back (`fallback`): repair when there is a plan, else redesign.

A failure with any diagnostic an earlier failure of the build had, consecutive or not (decision D124), ends in `failed` `{reason: "no-progress"}` with those diagnostics and, when a check rejected a draft, its `scxml`; at the request's `max_attempts` failures it ends in `failed` `{reason: "attempts-exhausted"}`.

Each check has its own diagnostics: a validator error (`kind` `validate`, its code), a draft that cannot be written (`draft` `write-failed`), test scripts out of bounds (`draft` `tests-out-of-bounds`, one to eight), and a test whose outputs or done differ from its expectations (`simulate` `test-failed`).

A generation that fails (`generate.failed`) is a `generate` diagnostic `<stage>-failed`; one that runs `generate_ceiling_ms` in all, or, once its reply streams, makes no progress for `generate_timeout_ms` (the first `generate.progress` arms it, each later one re-arms it), is cancelled, a `timeout` diagnostic `<stage>-timeout` (decision D101).

With the request's lifetime bounds (`min_every_ms`, `turn_after_bound_ms`), a draft that sends `bot.behavior.tick` (a persistent routine) whose schedule is shorter than `min_every_ms` is a `lifetime` diagnostic `E0009`; a routine within the bounds also gets a forced first tick, whose output must select at least one event (else an `apply` diagnostic `E0008`).

With the request's `apply` `{turn, input, targets}`, a draft that sends no `bot.behavior.tick` also runs once with the params `turn` and `input` (the simulation result `live turn`) and must end within min(`turn_after_bound_ms`, 2000) ms in a top-level final state whose donedata is `{turn, handled: true, selected}` with the live turn and selections naming targets among `targets` with data agreeing with `input`, else an `apply` diagnostic `E0008` (`<behavior:verify_apply>`, decision D131).

With the request's `template` `'turn'` (it then requires `name` and `apply`; decision D132) there is no `design`: the plan is the turn behavior template's, `author` asks for `turn_script` `{lifetime, script, tests}`, the chart written is the template naming `<name>.js` (`<behavior:turn_program>`) and `<name>.json` is `{"$defs":{}}`; the simulation runs the live turn, then each test input the same way, and a test input whose `handled` is false must not be answered (else an `apply` diagnostic `E0008` naming the test); a `turn_script` whose `lifetime` is `persistent` is planned and authored once as a whole document (`scxml_draft`).
